one_line_contribution: An offline audit showing that in a four-writer ALFWorld experience store a plain retriever over-retrieves items written by the reader's own policy when the query contains the reader's own trajectory text (surviving canonicalisation of scaffold formatting), plus a costed comparison showing that re-ranking by each writer's per-type collection success beats uniform retrieval and proximity weighting while reader-side calibration adds little and transfers.
closest_prior_work: Verified via s2cli: Sigma-Mem, 'An Online Reliability Memory for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems' (arXiv:2607.27958, 2026-07-30, verified by id) is the closest threat to the explicit half. It states the same premise almost verbatim - existing memory systems preserve interaction content 'rather than modeling which agents can be trusted and under what conditions' - and builds an online per-peer competence/reliability memory used to condition on peers. It does not threaten the implicit half (retrieved share by writer identity) and does not cost trust weighting against uniform retrieval on a task benchmark, but a reviewer will ask why 'trust should follow the writer's type-level record' is a new claim rather than the operating assumption of this line. Also verified: SuperLocalMemory (arXiv:2603.02240, 2026-02-17, cit 8) already pairs Bayesian trust scoring with adaptive learning-to-rank over a multi-agent store - the proposal's distinction is only that its writers are benign rather than poisoned; MAP-Graph (arXiv:2608.10509, 2026-08-11, cit 6) already promotes provenance from audit metadata to an operational control signal; MATM (arXiv:2606.19911, verified, cit 0) supplies the producer/consumer store. On the implicit half I found nothing that measures retrieved share by writer identity in a mixed agent store; the nearest are the IR source-bias papers the proposal already cites (2602.10833 and 2604.06163, both verified by id), which establish that the retriever-side prior exists but attribute it to training data and non-semantic surface features, not to authorship by the querying policy. That gap is real, and it is where essentially all of this proposal's novelty sits.
strongest_objection: The share audit's null is wrong, so the headline word 'homophily' is not what the design measures. P1 scores the self writer's retrieved share against its 0.25 store share, but under Q-traj the query literally contains the reader's own first three steps, and the self writer's items are on-policy successes of that same policy on the same environment - they share state sequences, object bindings and action orderings with the reader's live rollout. Over-retrieval of them is then the retriever behaving correctly under a relevance notion the proposal has not ruled out, not a bias; the canonical-format arm removes surface style but strengthens rather than removes this confound, because canonicalisation leaves exactly the actions and observations that are genuinely shared. Without a usefulness-matched null (e.g. per-item downstream gain, or a permutation null over writers matched on state overlap), a 0.15 excess is uninterpretable, and the proposal's own framing concedes as much by conditioning P2 on the types where a foreign writer is better - which is the only place a self-preference could be costly, so 'homophily costs the reader six net points' is arranged by type selection rather than discovered. Secondary but nearly as damaging: P4's headline 'calibration adds little' is manufactured by the design the entailment check already flagged (c=20 episodes per writer x type gives SE ~ 0.11 on each weight, so the calibrated weights are noise), and its >= 70 percent retention ratio has a denominator the same prediction asserts is near zero; the proposal was told this and did not raise c or add an oracle reader-side ceiling.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Replace the 0.25 store-share null in P1 with a usefulness null: for a sample of retrievals, measure each candidate item's actual downstream contribution (leave-one-in at k=1, or a held-out per-item gain estimate) and report self-share excess relative to the share an oracle-usefulness ranker would give the self writer. Bias is the residual, and only that residual supports the word homophily. (2) Add the item-level control described under missing_baseline and report whether writer identity carries any signal beyond it. (3) Fix P4: raise c to ~100 games per writer x type, report the sampling error of the weights, add an oracle reader-side weighting fitted on validation as the ceiling, and pre-register a floor on the matched calibration gain below which the transfer ratio is not computed. (4) Fix P5's denominator by choosing the comparator single-writer store on the 60-game train slice and scoring it on validation, and state the ratio's CI half-width rather than a 0.9/1.0 threshold that is ~2 net points wide. (5) Either secure gpt-oss-120b before pre-registration or drop the capability axis honestly: EXAONE-4.0-32B is the same size as Qwen3-32B, so the fallback converts 'capability varied at fixed proximity' into 'family varied at fixed capability', which is the exact confound the brief makes binding. (6) Move the decision thresholds off 6 net or buy the seeds: with paired CIs at about +/-4.5 the 4-to-6 band that decides P2 and P3 is inside the noise.
missing_baseline: Item-level quality re-ranking with writer identity removed - boost by properties of the individual trajectory (success/failure label, number of steps relative to the expert-optimal length for that task, or a learned per-item utility score in the style of utility-based retrieval, arXiv:2504.00573) with no provenance tag at all. The whole proposal presupposes that the writer is the right unit of trust; a per-item quality signal is cheaper than the writer-side statistic, needs no provenance infrastructure, and is the arm that decides whether 'who wrote it' adds anything over 'how good is this item'. If item-level weighting matches per-type writer-side weighting, P3 survives numerically but the paper's thesis does not. A second, cheaper omission: hard per-type writer selection using the same s_w(t) (keep only the best writer's items for each type) as the feasible counterpart of the oracle-best-single-writer bound - the alpha sweep approaches this in the limit but it is never named as a comparator, and if hard selection ties the soft re-ranker the contribution reduces to store filtering.
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central claim. The proposal's own check is unusually good by the standards of this round - three classed queries, IDs, hit counts, an explicit statement that WebSearch was unavailable, and a verdict that names the nearest mechanism (2602.10833, 2604.06163) rather than claiming a clean field - and I credit it. My own searches, all channel (a) s2cli (S2 ok, HF ok; WebSearch is unavailable in this session, so no section-text follow-up was possible for any query): [q1, --recent] 'retriever prefers items written by the querying agent itself self-authored memory retrieval share' - 13 hits, none on writer identity in retrieval; nearest 2603.02473 (retrieval vs utilization bottlenecks in agent memory) and 2606.04315. [q2] 'trust weighting writer capability shared experience store multi-agent memory retrieval provenance reranking' - 15 hits, and this returned the paper the proposal's own check missed: 2607.27958 Sigma-Mem (online reliability memory modelling which agents can be trusted and under what conditions), plus 2607.24117 (graded transmitter reliability for routing/quarantine in multi-agent claim chains), 2606.25161 TRUSTMEM, 2601.21742 (peer reliability estimation), 2602.16493 MMA (dynamic memory reliability scoring). None measures retrieved share by writer or costs trust weighting against uniform retrieval on benign writers, but four of these five post-date or sit alongside the cited MAP-Graph/SuperLocalMemory and the check did not surface the reliability-memory line at all. [q3, --recent] 'self-preference bias LLM own generated text retrieval homophily authorship' - 7 hits, all judge-side or generation-side self-preference (2410.21819, 2506.02592, 2602.15456 'In Agents We Trust, but Who Do Agents Trust? Latent Source Preferences Steer LLM Generations', 2601.03746); nothing on retrieval of one's own trajectories. [q4] home literature, 'weighting demonstrators by demonstration quality success rate imitation from heterogeneous suboptimal demonstrators' - 12 hits; 2606.05588 'Auditing Demonstration Curation Metrics' is directly relevant to the missing item-level baseline (action-only scorers fail on structural defects; high detection accuracy does not imply improved policy) and is uncited. [q5, --recent] 'per-task competence score routing which agent memory to reuse task-type success rate weighting retrieval' - 12 hits, nearest 2603.22455 SkillRouter and 2608.22695 Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (retrieve-then-rank over capability registries), neither on provenance trust. ID verification: I verified 2608.10509, 2603.02240, 2606.19911, 2602.10833, 2604.06163 and 2607.27958 by id on S2.
